entities.summary: Lewis of Luxembourg was a pivotal figure in Western Europe during the Medieval era. As the Bishop of Therouanne from 1415 to 1436, he played a crucial role in shaping the religious and political landscape of the region. His appointment as Archbishop of Rouen in 1436 further solidified his influence, while his subsequent appointment as Bishop of Ely in 1437 marked a significant shift in his ecclesiastical career. As a cardinal, Lewis of Luxembourg was a key player in the development of the Catholic Church's hierarchy during this period. He died on September 27, 1443, leaving behind a legacy that continues to be studied by historians today. The legacy of Lewis of Luxembourg can be seen in the numerous ecclesiastical institutions he founded, including the Collegiate Church of Saint-Pierre in Therouanne, which remains an important cultural landmark in the region. The impact of his religious and political influence can be seen in the subsequent appointment of his successors, who continued to shape the course of Western European history. Lewis of Luxembourg's life and career serve as a testament to the enduring power of the Catholic Church in shaping the course of human events. The influence of his legacy can be seen in the numerous historical accounts of his life and reign, which continue to be written and studied by scholars today.
